paper.title: Rethinking Muon Beyond Pretraining: Spectral Failures and High-Pass Remedies for VLA and RLVR
paper.abstract: Muon is a matrix-aware optimizer that leverages Newton-Schulz (NS) iterations to enforce spectral gradient orthogonalization by driving all singular values of the momentum matrix toward 1. While this uniform spectral whitening enhances exploration and outperforms AdamW in LLM pretraining, we show it could lead to fundamental limitations beyond pretraining in two regimes: (i) cross-modality vision-language-action (VLA) training, where inherently low-rank action-module gradients cause amplificatio

summary.core_problem: 矩阵感知优化器Muon在LLM预训练中表现优于AdamW，但其核心的统一谱白化机制会将动量矩阵的所有奇异值推向1，在预训练之外的两个关键场景存在本质缺陷：1）跨模态视觉-语言-动作（VLA）训练中，动作模块梯度本身低秩，尾部分量以噪声为主，Muon会放大这些噪声方向；2）带可验证奖励的强化学习后训练（RLVR）中，梯度信噪比低且需要保留预训练习得的注意力头分工，统一白化会导致更新不稳定。现有低秩Muon变体依赖固定秩截断和额外SVD/随机投影开销，无法适配不同层和训练阶段的动态需求。
summary.importance: 首次系统揭示了Muon类矩阵优化器在预训练后场景的谱特性缺陷，提出的Pion优化器可直接作为Muon的 drop-in 替换，计算开销与Muon完全一致，在多模态和RL后训练场景均取得稳定收益，为大模型全链路训练（预训练→多模态适配→RL对齐）的优化器选型和设计提供了核心依据。
summary.technical_approach: 提出Pion（动量谱高通优化器），核心是利用Newton-Schulz（NS）迭代的多项式结构，将Muon的单阶段谱白化改造为两阶段的Promotion+Suppression多项式映射（高通NS）：首先放大主导奇异值，再抑制尾部奇异值，形成软高通滤波器，将前导有效奇异值锚定在1的同时把噪声尾部推向0，每步计算开销与Muon完全相同。进一步引入分头模式，将注意力投影矩阵按头维度拆分，对每个头独立执行高通NS迭代，适配不同注意力头的更新尺度差异，无额外计算开销。
summary.experiments: 在VLA任务上，基于π0.5骨干模型，在LIBERO、LIBERO-Plus数据集和真实Franka机器人平台上，带ℓ1回归和流匹配头的训练中，Pion效果超过AdamW和Muon；在RLVR任务上，基于Qwen3-1.7B/4B模型，使用GRPO、GMPO算法在MATH和GSM8K数据集上，Pion同样稳定优于AdamW和Muon，同时保持与Muon相同的计算效率。消融实验验证了高通NS和分头模式的各自贡献。
summary.reading_guide: 重点阅读第2章对Muon谱缺陷的分析、第3章Pion的高通NS设计，以及第4章的VLA和RLVR实验对比，附录中的多项式系数推导细节可深入参考。核心创新点在于利用NS迭代的多项式结构实现无额外开销的谱高通滤波，而非依赖SVD等重计算操作。值得深挖的方向包括将高通NS机制适配到预训练场景，以及针对不同训练阶段动态调整高通滤波器的截止阈值。

summary_en.core_problem: The matrix-aware optimizer Muon outperforms AdamW in LLM pretraining, but its core uniform spectral whitening mechanism that pushes all singular values of the momentum matrix to 1 has fundamental limitations in two critical post-pretraining regimes: 1) Cross-modality Vision-Language-Action (VLA) training, where action module gradients are inherently low-rank with noise-dominated tail components, which Muon amplifies; 2) Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) post-training, where gradients have low SNR and attention head specialization inherited from pretraining needs to be preserved, making uniform whitening unstable. Existing low-rank Muon variants rely on fixed-rank truncation and extra SVD/random projection overhead, and cannot adapt to dynamic requirements across layers and training steps.
summary_en.importance: First systematically reveals the spectral limitations of Muon-style matrix optimizers in post-pretraining scenarios. The proposed Pion optimizer is a direct drop-in replacement for Muon with identical computational cost, delivering consistent gains in both multimodal and RL post-training. It provides core guidance for optimizer selection and design across the full LLM training pipeline: pretraining → multimodal adaptation → RL alignment.
summary_en.technical_approach: Proposes Pion (Spectral High-pass Optimization on Momentum). Leveraging the polynomial structure of Newton-Schulz (NS) iteration, it reformulates Muon's single-stage spectral whitening into a two-stage Promotion+Suppression polynomial map (high-pass NS): it first amplifies dominant singular values, then suppresses tail components, forming a soft high-pass filter that anchors informative leading singular values at 1 while driving noisy tails toward 0, with identical per-step computational cost as Muon. A per-head mode is further introduced, which splits attention projection matrices along the head dimension and runs high-pass NS iteration independently for each head, adapting to heterogeneous update scales across attention heads with no additional overhead.
summary_en.experiments: On VLA tasks with π0.5 backbone, Pion outperforms AdamW and Muon on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus datasets and real Franka robot setups with ℓ1 regression and flow-matching heads. On RLVR tasks with Qwen3-1.7B/4B using GRPO and GMPO algorithms on MATH and GSM8K, Pion also consistently outperforms AdamW and Muon while matching Muon's computational efficiency. Ablation studies verify the individual contributions of high-pass NS and per-head mode.
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus on Section 2 for analysis of Muon's spectral defects, Section 3 for Pion's high-pass NS design, and Section 4 for VLA and RLVR experimental comparisons. Refer to the appendix for polynomial coefficient derivation details. The core innovation is leveraging the polynomial structure of NS iteration to achieve overhead-free spectral high-pass filtering, instead of relying on expensive operations like SVD. Worthwhile follow-up directions include adapting the high-pass NS mechanism to pretraining scenarios, and dynamically adjusting the high-pass filter cutoff threshold across training stages.

recommendation.zh: Muon 不能直接平移到 RLVR/VLA；应优先看谱分析和 Pion ablation，内部后训练优化器实验值得复现。
recommendation.en: Muon does not transfer cleanly to RLVR/VLA; read the spectral analysis and Pion ablations, then reproduce the optimizer swap internally.

paper.title: Muon is Not That Special: Random or Inverted Spectra Work Just as Well
paper.abstract: The recent empirical success of the Muon optimizer has renewed interest in non-Euclidean optimization, typically justified by similarities with second-order methods, and linear minimization oracle (LMO) theory. In this paper, we challenge this geometric narrative through three contributions, demonstrating that precise geometric structure is not the key factor affecting optimization performance. First, we introduce Freon, a family of optimizers based on Schatten (quasi-)norms, powered by a novel,

summary.core_problem: Muon这类谱优化器此前被普遍认为性能来源于严格的非欧几何预条件和线性最小化预言机（LMO）理论要求的精确几何结构，近期已有实验证据与该理论叙事出现矛盾，核心待解决问题是明确谱优化器性能提升的真实驱动因素，而非停留在几何框架的表面解释。
summary.importance: 修正了大模型预训练优化器的基础理论认知，推翻了精确几何结构是谱优化器性能核心的主流假设，打开了更宽的优化器设计空间。提出的Freon优化器族为预训练优化器选型和调参提供了新的可行选项，梯度对齐度与下降势能的分解框架提供了量化解释优化器 tradeoff 的机制，直接指导后续大模型预训练优化方向的研究。
summary.technical_approach: 首先提出Freon优化器族，更新形式为(GG⊤)^{-c}G，c=0对应SGD，c=1/2对应Muon，c≥1/2时进入Schatten准范数区域，该区域超出了标准LMO理论的覆盖范围。为稳定计算该更新，设计了基于QDWH极分解的可证明最优迭代近似算法，扩展了此前的极分解优化理论。其次提出Kaon优化器：完全不计算LMO、不瞄准任何Schatten范数，仅将梯度的奇异值替换为随机噪声，同时保留大奇异值被抑制的特性。最后扩展了已有分解框架，将局部泰勒展开拆分为批量梯度对齐度γ_k和方向下降势能Φ_k两个可解释指标，揭示了不同优化器的核心权衡：牺牲多少梯度对齐度换取更高的下降势能，而最终收益能否实现取决于步长是否适配。与现有方法的核心区别是：现有谱优化器均在LMO框架下追求精确几何结构，该工作完全跳出该框架，证明精确几何结构无关紧要，核心有效机制是大奇异值抑制。
summary.experiments: 在GPT-2预训练任务上对Freon的c参数做扫参，最优值严格集中在c∈[0.5,1]的准范数区域，该范围无法被标准LMO理论解释，直接证伪了原有理论的普适性。所有c>0的Freon变体，以及完全随机谱的Kaon优化器，只要大奇异值被充分抑制，性能都与Muon高度接近。奇异值谱的精确形状对最终训练性能的影响可忽略。通过γ_k和Φ_k的分解验证了核心权衡：谱优化器牺牲了部分梯度对齐度，换来了更高的下降势能，配合调优后的步长即可实现超过AdamW的性能。Kaon与Muon的最终困惑度差异在统计误差范围内，二者均稳定优于AdamW。
summary.reading_guide: 重点读第2章的理论分析部分，尤其是Theorem2.1（准范数区域违反LMO假设的证明）、Theorem2.6（c≥1/2区域的对称性分析）、Theorem2.7（QDWH迭代的最优性证明），理解Freon的理论基础。接着读第3章的分解框架，明确优化器性能差异的底层解释。优先看Figure3、4、6，分别是不同优化器的性能对比、c参数扫参结果，直观验证几何结构无关的核心结论。附录中的Algorithm2（Kaon实现）和Algorithm3（QDWH迭代实现）可直接参考复现用于实际预训练。值得深挖的方向包括：LLaMA、MoE等不同架构下最优c参数的分布规律、训练过程中大奇异值抑制强度的动态调度策略、Kaon类随机谱优化器的速度和内存优化方案。

summary_en.core_problem: Prevailing narratives attribute the performance of spectral optimizers like Muon to strict non-Euclidean preconditioning and exact adherence to Linear Minimization Oracle (LMO) theory. Recent empirical inconsistencies contradict this geometric framing. The core open question is identifying the actual driver of spectral optimizer performance, rather than relying on surface-level geometric explanations.
summary_en.importance: These findings revise the foundational theoretical understanding of large-scale pre-training optimizers. The core assumption that precise geometric structure is required for strong spectral optimizer performance is invalidated, opening a much broader design space for optimizer development. The proposed optimizer families provide practical new options for pre-training tuning, and the proposed decomposition framework offers a quantitative mechanism to explain optimizer tradeoffs, directly guiding future optimization research for large language models.
summary_en.technical_approach: First, the Freon optimizer family is introduced, with update rule (GG⊤)^{-c}G, interpolating between SGD (c=0) and Muon (c=1/2), and extending into the Schatten quasi-norm regime for c≥1/2, which falls outside the coverage of standard LMO theory. A provably optimal QDWH-based iterative approximation algorithm is developed to compute these updates stably, extending prior polar decomposition optimization theory. Second, the Kaon optimizer is proposed: it does not compute any LMO or target a specific Schatten norm, and simply replaces the singular values of the gradient with random noise, while retaining suppression of large singular values. Third, a prior decomposition framework is extended to split local Taylor expansions into two interpretable metrics: batch gradient alignment (γ_k) and directional descent potential (Φ_k), exposing the core tradeoff across optimizers: how much gradient alignment is sacrificed to gain higher descent potential, with realized performance dependent on step size tuning.
summary_en.experiments: On GPT-2 pre-training tasks, parameter sweeps over Freon's c value show optimal settings concentrate strictly in the quasi-norm regime c ∈ [0.5, 1], a range that cannot be explained by standard LMO theory. All Freon variants with c>0 and the random-spectrum Kaon optimizer achieve nearly identical performance to Muon, as long as large singular values are sufficiently suppressed. The exact shape of the singular value spectrum has negligible impact on final training performance. Decomposition into γ_k and Φ_k confirms the core tradeoff: spectral optimizers sacrifice partial gradient alignment for higher descent potential, which translates to better performance when paired with appropriately tuned step sizes. Final perplexity gaps between Kaon and Muon fall within statistical error, and both outperform AdamW by a consistent margin.
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus first on Section 2 for theoretical analysis, particularly Theorem 2.1 (proof that the quasi-norm regime violates LMO assumptions), Theorem 2.6 (symmetry analysis for c≥1/2), and Theorem 2.7 (optimality proof for the QDWH iteration). Next read Section 3 for the decomposition framework explaining optimizer tradeoffs. Prioritize Figures 3, 4, and 6 for empirical validation of the core claim that geometric structure is irrelevant. Review Algorithm 2 (Kaon) and Algorithm 3 (QDWH iteration) in appendices for implementable details. Key directions for further exploration include: the distribution of optimal c across model architectures like LLaMA and MoE, dynamic scheduling of singular value suppression strength across training stages, and efficiency optimizations for Kaon-style random-spectrum optimizers for large-scale pre-training.

recommendation.zh: 直接推翻了Muon优化器的几何归因，做预训练优化器的研究员必须复现§4的GPT-2实验，结论直接影响优化选型
recommendation.en: Directly undermines the geometric justification of the Muon optimizer; pretrain researchers working on optimizers must replicate the GPT-2 experiments in §4 as the conclusion directly impacts optimizer selection

paper.title: Gradient Clipping Beyond Vector Norms: A Spectral Approach for Matrix-Valued Parameters
paper.abstract: Gradient clipping is a standard safeguard for training neural networks under noisy, heavy-tailed stochastic gradients; yet, most clipping rules treat all parameters as vectors and ignore the matrix structure of modern architectures. We show empirically that data outliers often amplify only a small number of leading singular values in layer-wise gradient matrices, while the rest of the spectrum remains largely unchanged. Motivated by this phenomenon, we propose spectral clipping, which stabilizes

summary.core_problem: 现有的梯度裁剪方法（如 norm clipping）将所有参数视为向量，忽略了现代深度学习模型参数的矩阵结构，导致在处理重尾噪声时不够精细。
summary.importance: 提出了一种利用参数矩阵结构的谱裁剪（spectral clipping）方法，为大模型预训练中的优化器设计提供了一个新的视角，有望在不增加过多计算开销的情况下提升训练稳定性。
summary.technical_approach: 作者观察到数据异常值通常只放大层级梯度矩阵的少数前导奇异值。基于此，谱裁剪方法在保留奇异方向的同时，对超过阈值的奇异值进行截断。该方法将经典的梯度范数裁剪作为特例，并可通过截断 SVD 高效实现。此外，作者还提出了基于指数移动平均或分位数的自适应阈值策略，以及逐层自适应裁剪方案。
summary.experiments: 在非凸优化下，证明了谱裁剪的收敛性，并在重尾噪声框架下建立了最优收敛率。实验表明，在 CIFAR-10 任务中，带有谱裁剪的 SGDM 优于带有范数裁剪的 SGDM。截断 SVD 的实现方式在保证精度的同时提高了效率。
summary.reading_guide: 建议重点关注 Section 2.2 的谱裁剪定义和 Section 5.2 的高效实现（Algorithm 2）。对于理论分析感兴趣的读者可以阅读 Section 3 的收敛性证明。预计阅读时间 20 分钟。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing gradient clipping methods treat all parameters as vectors, ignoring the matrix structure of modern deep learning models, which leads to suboptimal handling of heavy-tailed noise.
summary_en.importance: Proposes a spectral clipping method that leverages the matrix structure of parameters, offering a new perspective for optimizer design in LLM pre-training and potentially improving training stability without excessive computational overhead.
summary_en.technical_approach: The authors observe that data outliers typically amplify only a few leading singular values of layer-wise gradient matrices. Based on this, spectral clipping clamps singular values exceeding a threshold while preserving singular directions. It generalizes classical gradient norm clipping and can be efficiently implemented via truncated SVD. Adaptive threshold strategies and layer-wise clipping schemes are also proposed.
summary_en.experiments: Convergence is proven for non-convex optimization, establishing an optimal rate under heavy-tailed noise. Experiments show SGDM with spectral clipping outperforms norm clipping on CIFAR-10. The truncated SVD implementation improves efficiency without sacrificing accuracy.
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus on Section 2.2 for the definition of spectral clipping and Section 5.2 for the efficient implementation (Algorithm 2). Readers interested in theory can review Section 3. Estimated reading time: 20 minutes.

recommendation.zh: 值得把 §实验中的谱分布图拿来对照内部 loss spike；若开销可控，应做一轮小规模 optimizer ablation。
recommendation.en: Compare its gradient spectra with internal loss-spike traces; if the overhead is tolerable, run a small optimizer ablation.

paper.title: OrScale: Orthogonalised Optimization with Layer-Wise Trust-Ratio Scaling
paper.abstract: Muon improves neural-network training by orthogonalizing matrix-valued updates, but it leaves each layer's update magnitude controlled mostly by a global learning rate. We introduce OrScale, a trust-ratio extension of Muon built on a simple rule: the denominator of a layer-wise ratio should measure the Frobenius norm of the actual parameter-space direction that will be applied. This yields OrScale for general matrix layers and OrScale-LM for language models, where Moonlight shape scaling is comb

summary.core_problem: Muon 优化器通过正交化更新方向，但缺乏像 LARS/LAMB 那样的逐层步长（magnitude）控制，导致在不同层（如注意力、MLP、投影层）梯度尺度差异大时，单一全局学习率无法最优地控制更新幅度。直接将 LAMB 移植到 Muon 会由于正交化丢失幅度信息而导致分母退化、动量截断饱和及权重范数失控。
summary.importance: 提出了一种原则性方法，将逐层信任比（trust-ratio）缩放引入正交化优化器（Muon），解决了 Muon 在 LLM 预训练中步长控制的缺陷。这使得 Muon 能够像 AdamW 一样稳定且高效地进行大规模预训练，并实现了学习率的无缝迁移。
summary.technical_approach: 提出了 OrScale 优化器，核心原则是：信任比的分母必须测量优化器实际从参数中减去的真实参数空间方向的 Frobenius 范数。具体而言，如果更新方向是 $\lambda W_{\ell} + s_{\ell}Q_{\ell}$（其中 $W_{\ell}$ 是权重，$Q_{\ell}$ 是正交化后的动量，$s_{\ell}$ 是形状因子），分母就应该精确测量这个表达式的范数。针对 LLM 预训练，提出了 OrScale-LM 变体，结合了 Moonlight 的形状因子 $s_{\ell} = 0.2\sqrt{\max(m_{\ell}, n_{\ell})}$ 和一个逐层校准常数，使得初始信任比严格为 1，从而直接继承 AdamW 调优好的学习率。
summary.experiments: 在 CIFAR-10/DavidNet 上，OrScale 在三个随机种子下均排名第一。在 125M 到 1.1B 参数规模的 FineWeb-Edu 预训练中，OrScale-LM 表现优于基线。消融实验验证了设计空间中其他变体确实会导致理论预测的失败模式（如分母退化、截断饱和）。
summary.reading_guide: 重点关注 Section 3 中关于信任比分母设计的核心原则，以及 Section 4 中对三种失败模式（分母退化、截断饱和、权重衰减失控）的理论与实证分析。Algorithm 1 给出了简洁的实现伪代码。

summary_en.core_problem: Muon optimizer orthogonalizes update directions but lacks layer-wise magnitude control like LARS/LAMB. A single global learning rate is suboptimal given the varying gradient scales across different layers (attention, MLP, projections). Naively porting LAMB to Muon fails because orthogonalization removes amplitude information, leading to degenerate denominators, clip-saturated momentum, and runaway weight norms.
summary_en.importance: Introduces a principled approach to incorporate layer-wise trust-ratio scaling into orthogonalized optimizers (Muon), addressing a key limitation in LLM pre-training. This enables Muon to train stably and efficiently at scale, with seamless learning rate transfer from AdamW.
summary_en.technical_approach: Proposes OrScale, built on the principle that the trust-ratio denominator must measure the Frobenius norm of the actual parameter-space direction subtracted from the weights. If the update is $\lambda W_{\ell} + s_{\ell}Q_{\ell}$ ($W_{\ell}$ is weight, $Q_{\ell}$ is orthogonalized momentum, $s_{\ell}$ is a shape factor), the denominator measures exactly this norm. For LLMs, OrScale-LM combines Moonlight's shape factor $s_{\ell} = 0.2\sqrt{\max(m_{\ell}, n_{\ell})}$ with a layer-wise calibration constant to ensure the initial trust ratio is exactly 1, allowing direct inheritance of AdamW-tuned learning rates.
summary_en.experiments: OrScale ranks first on CIFAR-10/DavidNet across three seeds. In FineWeb-Edu pre-training (125M to 1.1B parameters), OrScale-LM outperforms baselines. Ablations confirm that alternative designs lead to predicted failure modes (degenerate denominators, clip saturation).
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus on Section 3 for the core principle of denominator design, and Section 4 for the theoretical and empirical analysis of the three failure modes. Algorithm 1 provides a concise implementation recipe.

recommendation.zh: 对Muon的一个扎实改进，关键insight是信任比分母应追踪实际更新方向而非代理度量。三种失败模式的分析很有价值，应纳入内部optimizer ablation考虑。
recommendation.en: A solid improvement on Muon with the key insight that trust-ratio denominators should track actual update directions. The three failure-mode analyses are valuable and should inform internal optimizer ablations.

paper.title: Pro-KLShampoo: Projected KL-Shampoo with Whitening Recovered by Orthogonalization
paper.abstract: Optimizers that exploit the matrix structure of gradients are central to modern LLM pre-training, with two distinct frontiers: explicit Kronecker-factored preconditioning -- most recently KL-Shampoo, which estimates the preconditioner via KL divergence minimization -- and orthogonalization of the gradient momentum, exemplified by Muon and analyzed as steepest descent under the spectral norm. The two routes are typically developed in isolation. We make a structural observation about KL-Shampoo's

summary.core_problem: KL-Shampoo等Kronecker预条件优化器在LLM预训练中效果优于AdamW，但计算和内存开销较大；同时Muon等正交化优化器与Kronecker预条件方法各自独立发展，缺乏统一框架。论文观察到KL-Shampoo的Kronecker预条件子特征值谱存在跨层、跨训练阶段都稳定的"尖峰-平坦"结构（少量主导特征值+近似均匀的尾部），但现有方法未利用此结构进行简化。
summary.importance: 对LLM预训练优化器研究有两点具体启发：（1）实证发现KL-Shampoo预条件子的spike-and-flat特征值结构是普遍现象，为优化器简化提供了结构性依据；（2）在低秩子空间上保留KL-Shampoo的精确预条件，在剩余方向上用正交化替代，既连接了Muon风格的正交化与KL估计框架，又降低了计算复杂度。该方法在验证损失、峰值内存和墙钟时间上均优于KL-Shampoo。
summary.technical_approach: 核心方案是将KL-Shampoo的一个Kronecker预条件子限制在与spike-and-flat结构对齐的参数化族中：对前r个主方向保持完整的谱估计，对剩余n-r个方向用单一共享特征值（标量尾部）近似。关键创新是将标量尾部更新替换为正交化操作——论文通过一个等式证明，在尾部方向上正交化可以恢复完整KL-Shampoo预条件子的代数形式，这不是启发式修补，而是有理论依据的等价转换。在低秩信号+噪声梯度模型下，该结构精确成立；论文还给出了算子范数光滑性假设下O(1/√T)的非凸收敛保证。
summary.experiments: 在GPT-2（124M/350M）和LLaMA（134M/450M）上进行了多组子空间秩r的对比实验。Pro-KLShampoo在所有配置下均优于KL-Shampoo：验证损失更低，峰值内存更小，达到相同损失水平的墙钟时间更短。包含消融实验以隔离每个设计组件的贡献。图1展示了跨层类型（attention/MLP）、跨深度（Layer 2/6/11）、跨训练阶段（Step 1500/3500）的特征值谱，证实spike-and-flat结构的普遍性。
summary.reading_guide: 重点看Section 1的结构观察和动机，Section 2的背景回顾（清晰梳理了K-FAC→Shampoo→KL-Shampoo的演进脉络），以及核心等式(12)（正交化恢复完整预条件子的证明）。图1的特征值谱可视化值得细看。实验部分主要看表格中的内存和时间对比。预计阅读时间：30-40分钟。
summary.authors_note: 预印本，作者机构未在提供内容中明确标注。

summary_en.core_problem: Kronecker preconditioned optimizers like KL-Shampoo outperform AdamW in LLM pretraining but incur higher compute and memory costs. Meanwhile, orthogonalization-based optimizers like Muon have developed in isolation from Kronecker methods. This paper identifies a universal 'spike-and-flat' eigenvalue structure in KL-Shampoo's Kronecker preconditioners—stable across layers and training stages—that is not exploited by existing methods.
summary_en.importance: Two concrete contributions for LLM pretraining optimizer research: (1) Empirical discovery that the spike-and-flat eigenvalue spectrum is a universal phenomenon in KL-Shampoo preconditioners, providing structural justification for optimizer simplification; (2) Replacing the scalar tail update with orthogonalization on the remaining directions, which connects Muon-style orthogonalization to the KL estimation framework while reducing complexity. Pro-KLShampoo improves over KL-Shampoo in validation loss, peak memory, and wallclock time across all tested configurations.
summary_en.technical_approach: The core idea is to restrict one of KL-Shampoo's Kronecker preconditioners to a parametric family aligned with the spike-and-flat structure: retain full spectral estimation on the top-r principal directions while approximating the remaining n-r directions with a single shared eigenvalue (scalar tail). The key innovation is replacing the scalar tail update with orthogonalization—Equation (12) proves that orthogonalization on the tail directions recovers the algebraic form of the full KL-Shampoo preconditioner, making this a theoretically justified equivalence rather than a heuristic. Under a rank-ρ signal-plus-noise gradient model, the spike-and-flat structure holds exactly. A nonconvex convergence guarantee of O(1/√T) is provided under operator-norm smoothness.
summary_en.experiments: Evaluated on GPT-2 (124M / 350M) and LLaMA (134M / 450M) across multiple subspace ranks. Pro-KLShampoo outperforms KL-Shampoo in all configurations: lower validation loss, smaller peak memory, and faster wallclock time to reach matched loss levels. Ablation studies isolate the contribution of each design component. Figure 1 visualizes eigenvalue spectra across layer types (attention/MLP), depths (Layer 2/6/11), and training stages (Step 1500/3500), confirming the universality of the spike-and-flat structure.
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus on Section 1 for the structural observation and motivation, Section 2 for the background (which provides a clear lineage from K-FAC to Shampoo to KL-Shampoo), and Equation (12) for the core equivalence proof. Figure 1's eigenvalue spectrum visualization is particularly informative. In the experiments section, prioritize the memory and timing comparison tables. Estimated reading time: 30-40 minutes.
summary_en.authors_note: Preprint. Author affiliations not explicitly stated in the provided content.

recommendation.zh: 优化器是预训练核心变量，这篇结合了KL-Shampoo与Muon两条路线的核心设计，可纳入内部优化器 ablation 参考。
recommendation.en: Optimizer is a core variable in LLM pretraining; this work combines core designs of KL-Shampoo and Muon lines, suitable for reference in internal optimizer ablations.

paper.title: Budget-aware Auto Optimizer Configurator
paper.abstract: Optimizer states occupy massive GPU memory in large-scale model training. However, gradients in different network blocks exhibit distinct behaviors, such as varying directional stability and scale anisotropy, implying that expensive optimizer states are not universally necessary and using a global optimizer is often memory-inefficient. We propose the Budget-Aware Optimizer Configurator (BAOC) to reduce memory cost by assigning suitable optimizer configurations to individual blocks under given bu

summary.core_problem: 论文解决的是大模型训练中优化器状态显存过高的问题。核心观察是：不同网络块的梯度行为并不相同，有的块方向稳定、适合动量累积；有的块尺度各向异性强、需要自适应缩放；有的块对低精度或去掉动量更耐受。现有 8-bit optimizer、Adafactor、GaLore 等方法通常把同一种优化器配置施加到全模型，容易在某些块上浪费状态显存，在另一些块上损害收敛。
summary.importance: 这篇工作的价值不在提出一个新的优化器，而在把“优化器怎么配”变成了一个可测量、可约束、可自动求解的分配问题。对预训练研究来说，这很实际：优化器状态是随参数量线性增长的长期显存开销，直接挤占 activation、batch size 和 sequence length 的空间。BAOC 给出的思路是只在需要的参数块上保留昂贵状态，把省下的显存换成更大的 batch、更长上下文或更低的并行压力。贡献量级更偏系统化和工程方法论，但切中大规模训练中的真实瓶颈。
summary.technical_approach: BAOC 将模型参数划分为 N 个不重叠 block，并为每个 block 从候选优化器配置集合中选择一个配置。这里的“配置”包括更新机制和状态精度，例如是否保留动量、是否使用自适应二阶统计、是否低精度存储状态等。流程分四步：第一，稀疏采样梯度流。每个 block 固定采样一小部分坐标，默认采样率 s=0.1%，训练中只记录这些坐标上的梯度序列，避免完整梯度统计带来的额外开销。第二，计算 block 级指标，例如方向稳定性、尺度各向异性和噪声相关信号。这些指标对应优化器机制的需求：方向稳定时动量更可能有效，尺度差异大时自适应缩放更有必要，波动强时便宜配置的风险更高。第三，把这些统计量映射成每个 block-配置组合的 mismatch risk。第四，求解带约束的混合整数线性规划：每个 block 必须选择一个配置，在总 optimizer-state memory 和相对 update time 预算内最小化总风险。论文对 StateMem 的定义比较严格，只统计优化器持有的持久状态张量，不包括模型参数、梯度、activation、临时 workspace、FP32 master weight 或 EMA 权重。时间预算则相对 AdamW16 归一化，并通过轻量 one-step timing 得到候选配置的相对更新成本。和全局低比特优化器或单一 Adafactor/GaLore 的区别是，BAOC 不假设某个便宜优化器适合所有层，而是把机制选择、精度选择和资源预算绑定起来做 block-wise allocation。
summary.experiments: 论文声称在 vision、language 和 diffusion workloads 上验证了 BAOC 的 memory-quality trade-off：在显著降低 optimizer-state memory 的同时维持训练质量。已给出的全文片段没有包含具体实验表格，因此不能可靠复述最终精度、loss、perplexity 或显存节省百分比。可确认的具体数字包括：梯度统计默认只采样每个 block 0.1% 的坐标；时间成本以 AdamW16 的 block 更新耗时为 1 做归一化；优化目标同时受 memory budget 和 time budget 约束。实验部分值得重点核对三类结果：同等显存预算下 BAOC 相比全局 8-bit/Adafactor/GaLore 的质量差距；同等质量下 optimizer-state memory 的节省；风险指标、采样率、block 粒度和 MILP 约束的消融。
summary.reading_guide: 建议精读方法部分的三个点。第一，看 StateMem 定义，因为它决定了论文声称的显存节省是否和实际训练显存一致；这里不包括 activation 和 master weights，解读实验时要分清 optimizer-state memory 与 end-to-end peak memory。第二，看 mismatch risk 如何从梯度统计映射到配置风险，这是方法是否可迁移到 LLM 预训练的关键。第三，看 MILP formulation，包括变量、目标函数、memory/time 约束和候选配置集合。实验部分优先看 memory-quality 曲线、同预算对比、block-wise assignment 可视化和 ablation。若只为 LLM 预训练落地，重点关注 language workload、采样开销、训练早期统计是否稳定，以及配置切换是否会引入 optimizer state warmup 问题。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper targets optimizer-state memory in large-scale training. Its main claim is that a single global optimizer configuration is often wasteful because gradient dynamics vary across parameter blocks. Some blocks benefit from momentum, some need adaptive scaling due to strong anisotropy, and some can tolerate lower precision or simpler updates. Applying one cheap optimizer everywhere saves memory but can damage sensitive blocks; applying Adam-style states everywhere spends memory where they are not needed.
summary_en.importance: The contribution is a practical allocation framework rather than a new optimizer. This matters for pretraining because optimizer states are persistent O(parameter) memory and compete directly with activations, batch size, sequence length, and parallelism choices. BAOC suggests a useful direction: retain expensive optimizer states only where gradient statistics justify them, and use cheaper configurations elsewhere. The impact is mainly methodological and systems-oriented, but it addresses a real scaling bottleneck in foundation-model training.
summary_en.technical_approach: BAOC partitions trainable parameters into N disjoint blocks and assigns one optimizer configuration to each block. A configuration combines update mechanism and state precision, such as momentum usage, adaptive statistics, and low-precision states. The pipeline has four stages. First, it samples sparse gradient streams from each block; the default sampling rate is 0.1% of coordinates, fixed after sampling. Second, it computes lightweight block-level metrics with running statistics, including signals such as directional stability, scale anisotropy, and noise. Third, it converts these metrics into a mismatch-risk score for each block-configuration pair. Fourth, it solves a constrained mixed-integer linear program that minimizes total risk while satisfying optimizer-state memory and update-time budgets. The memory definition is careful: it counts only persistent optimizer-owned state tensors and excludes parameters, gradients, activations, scratch buffers, FP32 master weights, and EMA copies. Update time is normalized against AdamW16 and estimated with a lightweight one-step timing measurement. The key difference from global 8-bit optimizers, Adafactor, or projection-based methods is that BAOC does not assume one low-memory mechanism is suitable for all layers.
summary_en.experiments: The supplied text states that BAOC is evaluated on vision, language, and diffusion workloads and achieves competitive memory-quality trade-offs with much lower optimizer-state memory. The provided full-content excerpt does not include the result tables, so exact loss, accuracy, perplexity, or memory-reduction numbers cannot be verified here. The concrete reported settings include a default sparse gradient sampling rate of 0.1%, update-time normalization to AdamW16, and a joint memory/time constrained allocation objective. The most important experimental evidence to inspect is the memory-quality frontier against global low-memory optimizers, quality retention under matched optimizer-state budgets, block-wise assignment patterns, and ablations over sampling rate, risk metrics, block granularity, and time constraints.
summary_en.reading_guide: Read the method section closely. The most important details are the optimizer-state memory definition, the gradient-derived risk metrics, and the MILP formulation. These determine whether the approach is merely a bookkeeping tool or a reliable training-time decision procedure. In the experiments, prioritize language-model results, memory-quality curves, assignment visualizations, and ablations on metric quality and sampling overhead. For pretraining use, check whether early gradient samples are stable enough, whether configurations are fixed or updated during training, and how optimizer states are initialized when a block receives a different configuration.

recommendation.zh: 应立刻看实验细节；若 blockwise optimizer 风险估计稳定，预训练预算分配不该再默认全层 AdamW。
recommendation.en: Read the experimental details now; if the blockwise optimizer-risk estimate is stable, full-model AdamW should no longer be the default budget allocation.

paper.title: A Self-Attentive Meta-Optimizer with Group-Adaptive Learning Rates and Weight Decay
paper.abstract: Adaptive optimizers like AdamW apply uniform hyperparameters across all parameter groups, ignoring heterogeneous optimization dynamics across layers and modules. We address this limitation by proposing MetaAdamW - a new optimizer that integrates a self-attention mechanism to dynamically modulate per-group learning rates and weight decay. The modulation factors are produced by a lightweight Transformer encoder that operates on statistical features (gradient norms, momentum norms, correlations) ex

summary.core_problem: 解决 AdamW 等自适应优化器对不同层和模块使用近似统一学习率、权重衰减时，无法适配异质优化动态的问题。
summary.importance: 贡献类型是优化器方法改进。它尝试用一个轻量 Transformer 作为 meta-optimizer，为参数组动态生成学习率和 weight decay 调制因子。对 LLM 预训练有概念相关性，但摘要显示实验主要是小规模多任务，离真实大模型预训练稳定性还有距离。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 MetaAdamW：从每个参数组提取梯度范数、动量范数、相关性等统计特征，输入 self-attention 模块，让参数组之间相互感知，再输出每组学习率和权重衰减的调制系数。训练该 attention module 的 meta-learning objective 结合 gradient alignment、loss decrease 和 generalization gap。另一个技术点是扩展 homoscedastic uncertainty weighting，引入 task-specific priorities 来调节正则项权重。
summary.experiments: 摘要提到在五类任务上实验，包括时间序列预测 ETT 和语言建模 Wiki 系列数据，但未给出模型规模、token 数、训练成本、baseline 完整列表或提升幅度。若实验停留在小模型，难以证明该优化器适合大规模 LLM 预训练。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses the limitation that AdamW-like optimizers use largely uniform learning-rate and weight-decay settings across parameter groups despite heterogeneous layer and module dynamics.
summary_en.importance: This is an optimizer-method contribution. It proposes a lightweight Transformer meta-optimizer that dynamically modulates per-group learning rates and weight decay. The idea is conceptually relevant to LLM pretraining, but the abstract suggests mostly small-scale multi-task experiments rather than convincing large-model pretraining evidence.
summary_en.technical_approach: MetaAdamW extracts statistical features from each parameter group, including gradient norms, momentum norms, and correlations. A self-attention module lets parameter groups condition on one another and outputs modulation factors for group-wise learning rate and weight decay. The attention module is trained with a meta-learning objective combining gradient alignment, loss decrease, and generalization gap. The paper also extends homoscedastic uncertainty weighting with task-specific priorities for regularization balancing.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract mentions five diverse tasks, including ETT time-series forecasting and Wiki language modeling, but does not provide model sizes, token budgets, training cost, full baselines, or gains. If the experiments are small-scale, they do not establish viability for large LLM pretraining.

recommendation.zh: 想法值得扫，但只看优化器定义和消融；没有大规模 LM 训练曲线前，不应替代 AdamW prior。
recommendation.en: Skim the optimizer definition and ablations only; without large-scale LM curves, it should not move the AdamW prior.

paper.title: Nora: Normalized Orthogonal Row Alignment for Scalable Matrix Optimizer
paper.abstract: Matrix-based optimizers have demonstrated immense potential in training Large Language Models (LLMs), however, designing an ideal optimizer remains a formidable challenge. A superior optimizer must satisfy three core desiderata: efficiency, achieving Muon-like preconditioning to accelerate optimization; stability, strictly adhering to the scale-invariance inherent in neural networks; and speed, minimizing computational overhead. While existing methods address these aspects to varying degrees, th

summary.core_problem: Nora 处理的是矩阵型优化器在 LLM 训练中的三方取舍：Muon 类正交化更新有较好的预条件效果，但 Newton-Schulz 迭代开销高；RMNP 类行归一化方法更快，但没有严格处理归一化网络中的尺度不变性，容易引入沿权重方向的径向扰动。论文希望得到一个同时满足预条件效率、尺度稳定性和低计算开销的矩阵优化器。
summary.importance: 这篇工作对预训练研究的价值主要在优化器设计。它把两个常被分开处理的问题合在一起：一是 Muon 式矩阵预条件能提升数据效率，二是 LayerNorm、RMSNorm 等结构使很多权重矩阵的有效学习发生在角向空间，而不是权重范数方向。Nora 的意义不在于提出复杂的新二阶方法，而在于给出一个很便宜的近似：先去掉行级径向动量，再做行级归一化。这个设计适合大规模训练，因为它关注的是每步额外开销、学习率可迁移性和训练稳定性，而不是只看少量 benchmark 的最终 loss。
summary.technical_approach: 方法的核心是 row-wise tangent update。给定权重矩阵 W 和动量 V，Nora 先把每一行动量分解为平行于对应权重行的分量和垂直分量，只保留垂直分量。这样更新方向在行级上与当前权重正交，减少不改变函数输出的径向噪声，也避免权重范数漂移导致有效学习率抖动。随后，Nora 对这个行级正交动量做归一化，用对角形式近似 Muon 的矩阵预条件。与 Muon 相比，它不需要 Newton-Schulz 迭代，避免了较高的矩阵计算开销；与 RMNP 相比，它不是直接归一化原始动量，而是先显式投影到尺度不变参数的切空间，因此更严格地满足 scale-invariance。论文还把 Nora 放到 μP 框架下分析，给出学习率随宽度缩放的条件，并提供非凸优化下的收敛保证。实际实现上，核心逻辑可以写成很短的矩阵代码，适合作为 Adam 或 momentum 类优化器的更新模块。
summary.experiments: 实验以 LLaMA 架构训练为主，覆盖不同模型规模和一组学习率设置，比较 Nora、Muon、RMNP 以及常规优化器的收敛速度和 wall-clock 表现。关键结论是：Nora 在训练 loss 下降速度上接近或优于 Muon 类矩阵预条件方法，同时由于只做行级投影和归一化，单步开销更低；相对 RMNP，Nora 在较大学习率或更长训练中更稳定，论文将其归因于去除了径向动量噪声。消融实验的重点应是两部分：只做行归一化但不做正交投影，会保留范数方向扰动；只做正交投影但不做预条件，收敛加速不足。全文材料中没有给出可核验的具体参数量、token 数或提升百分比，因此不宜把实验量级解读得过重。
summary.reading_guide: 建议泛读，约 30–45 分钟。优先看 Nora Optimizer 一节，重点是动量的行级正交投影公式和后续归一化步骤；再看 μP scaling 相关定理，判断它的学习率缩放假设是否适合自己的训练配置；最后看 LLaMA 训练曲线、学习率 sweep 和 wall-clock 对比。精力有限时，可以跳过较长的非凸收敛证明，只保留结论条件。值得深挖的是它对尺度不变性的处理：如果训练栈中大量使用 RMSNorm/LayerNorm，这类切空间更新可能比单纯追求更强预条件更稳。

summary_en.core_problem: Nora addresses a practical trade-off in matrix-based optimizers for LLM training. Muon-style orthogonalized updates provide useful matrix preconditioning but rely on Newton-Schulz iterations and add noticeable compute overhead. RMNP-style row normalization is much cheaper, but it does not strictly respect the scale-invariant geometry induced by normalization layers, so radial momentum noise can perturb weight norms and the effective learning rate.
summary_en.importance: The main relevance is optimizer design for large-scale pretraining. The paper connects two issues that are often treated separately: matrix preconditioning for data efficiency, and tangent-space updates for scale-invariant parameters. Nora is useful because it proposes a cheap approximation rather than a heavier second-order method. It aims to preserve most of the benefit of Muon-like updates while controlling per-step overhead and reducing norm-direction jitter.
summary_en.technical_approach: The method uses row-wise tangent updates. For a weight matrix W and momentum V, Nora decomposes each momentum row into the component parallel to the corresponding weight row and the component orthogonal to it. It discards the parallel component and updates only with the row-wise orthogonal momentum. This removes radial motion that does not change the function for scale-invariant weights. Nora then applies a diagonal preconditioning estimate through row-wise normalization, which approximates the effect of a Muon-like matrix preconditioner without Newton-Schulz iterations. Compared with Muon, the method is much cheaper. Compared with RMNP, it first projects into the tangent space and therefore treats scale invariance more explicitly. The paper also analyzes learning-rate scaling under the μP framework and gives non-convex convergence guarantees.
summary_en.experiments: The experiments train LLaMA-style models at multiple scales and across learning-rate sweeps, comparing Nora with Muon, RMNP, and standard optimizers. The reported pattern is that Nora improves convergence speed while keeping wall-clock cost lower than heavier matrix optimizers. It is also more stable than plain row-wise momentum normalization, especially when learning-rate sensitivity and weight-norm drift matter. The most informative ablations are the separation between row-wise orthogonal projection and row-wise normalization: projection controls radial noise, while normalization provides the cheap preconditioning effect. The provided material does not expose reliable exact numbers for model sizes, token counts, or percentage gains, so the empirical magnitude should be interpreted with care.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim in about 30–45 minutes. Read the optimizer section first, especially the formula for row-wise projection and the subsequent normalization step. Then inspect the μP scaling arguments to see whether the proposed learning-rate rules match your own parameterization. Finally, focus on the LLaMA training curves, learning-rate sweeps, wall-clock comparison, and ablations. The convergence proof can be read selectively unless the assumptions are directly relevant to your optimizer work.

recommendation.zh: 值得看方法节和稳定性实验；如果投影约束真能压住 norm jitter，应放进内部 optimizer ablation。
recommendation.en: Read the method and stability plots; if the projection really suppresses norm jitter, it deserves an internal optimizer ablation.

paper.title: Anon: Extrapolating Optimizer Adaptivity Across the Real Spectrum
paper.abstract: Adaptive optimizers such as Adam have achieved great success in training large-scale models like large language models and diffusion models. However, they often generalize worse than non-adaptive methods, such as SGD on classical architectures like CNNs. We identify a key cause of this performance gap: adaptivity in pre-conditioners, which limits the optimizer's ability to adapt to diverse optimization landscapes. To address this, we propose Anon (Adaptivity Non-restricted Optimizer with Novel c

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作讨论的是一个老问题，但切口比较新：为什么 Adam 一类自适应优化器在大模型训练里几乎是默认选择，却常常比 SGD 更容易带来泛化损失，而且不同模型家族之间很难有一个统一好用的优化器。作者把问题收束到 pre-conditioner 的“适应性强度”上，也就是梯度缩放变化时，预条件矩阵会跟着变化多少。现有方法把这个强度基本固定死了：SGD 接近 0，Adam/RMSProp 接近 1。作者认为这会让优化器对某类梯度统计过度匹配，换到另一类训练景观时就不合适，因此提出把 adaptivity 作为一个连续可调的控制变量，而不是离散地在 SGD 和 Adam 之间二选一。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的意义主要有两层。第一，它试图把“为什么 Adam 适合 LLM、SGD 常在 CNN 上泛化更好”这类经验事实，重新表述成一个可分析、可调参、可统一的优化器设计维度。这比单纯再造一个 optimizer 更有研究价值，因为它给了一个解释框架。第二，它提出的可调 adaptivity 如果在大规模语言模型上也成立，潜在价值在于：不同训练阶段、不同数据混合、不同参数子空间，可能并不需要同一种固定的预条件强度。这个方向和 pretrain 中越来越常见的阶段化训练、cooldown、mid-training recipe 调整是相容的。不过从给出的内容看，这篇更像优化器理论与通用深度学习训练的统一尝试，对 LLM 预训练的直接证据还不算充分，启发大于定论。
summary.technical_approach: 方法上有两个关键点。第一，作者给出一个统一的 adaptivity 定义，用 pre-conditioner 对全局梯度缩放的对数敏感度来刻画优化器的“自适应程度”。在这个定义下，SGD、RMSProp、Adam 都可以放到同一条连续谱上。然后他们提出 Anon，用一个实数超参 γ 来控制 adaptivity，允许 γ 取整个实数域，而不只是 0 到 1 之间。这样它既能在 SGD-like 和 Adam-like 行为之间插值，也允许向两端外推。第二，作者注意到当 γ 过大或为负时，预条件器会出现明显的稳定性问题，传统 AMSGrad 那种 hard max-tracking 不足以覆盖这种更广的 adaptivity 范围，于是提出 incremental delay update, IDU。按文中描述，IDU 不是简单地对二阶统计做最大值截断，而是用一种更平滑、分层延迟的累积机制来控制预条件器的变化速度，从而在极端 adaptivity 下仍保持收敛。理论部分给了 online convex 和 stochastic non-convex 两类设置下的收敛分析，重点是在全 adaptivity spectrum 上建立稳定性，而不是只证明某个特例。和已有方法相比，这篇的区别不在于又换了一种二阶矩估计，而在于把“预条件器对梯度尺度的响应强度”提升为一等设计对象，并围绕这个对象重写了优化器家族的参数化方式。
summary.experiments: 从提供的全文片段看，实验覆盖图像分类、语言建模和生成建模三类任务，作者声称 Anon 在不同架构上都优于强基线，并把这作为“通用优化器”的证据。不过当前可见内容没有给出足够完整的表格数字，尤其缺少你会关心的几类关键信息：语言模型的参数规模、训练 token 数、与 AdamW 的 loss/perplexity 差距、最终下游差异，以及 γ 的最优区间是否随模型和阶段变化。能确认的是，作者做了两类重要验证：一类是 adaptivity 连续变化时的性能曲线，用来支持“固定 adaptivity 不是最优”的论点；另一类是 IDU 与 AMSGrad 式稳定化手段的比较，用来说明当 γ 超出常规范围时，IDU 更能避免发散。若后文完整实验里包含 LLM 或 diffusion 的大规模训练曲线，这部分值得重点看；否则这篇更适合作为优化器设计思想参考，而不是直接改 pretrain recipe 的依据。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读建议是先抓三处。第一看第 2.2 节 adaptivity 的定义，这决定了整篇文章是否只是重新命名旧现象，还是确实给了一个有区分度的新坐标系。第二看第 3.1 节 Anon 的更新式，重点弄清 γ 到底如何进入 pre-conditioner，以及 γ<0、γ>1 时更新在直觉上分别意味着什么。第三看第 3.3 节 IDU 和理论部分，判断它是不是一个真正必要的新稳定化机制，还是对已有 max-tracking 的变体包装。实验部分建议优先看不同任务上最优 γ 的分布、对学习率和 weight decay 的耦合敏感性、以及是否存在训练前期和后期偏好不同 adaptivity 的现象。预计 30 到 45 分钟可以完成一次有效泛读；如果你做 optimizer for pretrain，值得再花时间把附录中的收敛条件和实现细节过一遍。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper revisits a familiar optimization gap from a more structural angle: adaptive methods such as Adam dominate large-scale training, including LLMs and diffusion models, yet they often generalize worse than SGD on other model families. The authors attribute a large part of this mismatch to the adaptivity of the pre-conditioner itself. Existing optimizers effectively hard-code a specific level of response to gradient statistics: SGD is near zero adaptivity, while Adam and RMSProp are near one. The claim is that this fixed choice can be misaligned with the optimization landscape of a given task or architecture, so adaptivity should be treated as a continuous design variable rather than a discrete optimizer identity.
summary_en.importance: For pretraining research, the main value is conceptual rather than immediately recipe-changing. The paper offers a cleaner lens for thinking about why Adam-like methods work well in large-scale language modeling while SGD-like behavior can still be preferable in other regimes. More importantly, it suggests that a single fixed pre-conditioning strength may be suboptimal across training stages, data mixtures, or parameter subspaces. That idea is relevant to staged pretraining, cooldown schedules, and optimizer transitions during long runs. Still, based on the visible content, the paper provides stronger evidence for a unified optimizer framework than for a decisive improvement in frontier-scale LLM pretraining.
summary_en.technical_approach: There are two central ingredients. First, the paper formalizes adaptivity as the log-sensitivity of the pre-conditioner to global gradient scaling. Under this view, SGD, RMSProp, and Adam become points on a single spectrum. The proposed optimizer, Anon, introduces a real-valued hyperparameter gamma that controls this adaptivity continuously over the full real line. This allows interpolation between SGD-like and Adam-like behavior, and also extrapolation beyond both. Second, the authors recognize that extreme adaptivity, especially gamma < 0 or gamma > 1, can destabilize training. To address this, they introduce incremental delay update, or IDU, a stabilization mechanism intended to replace hard max-tracking such as AMSGrad. Instead of simply clipping the second-moment statistics through a running maximum, IDU appears to use a softer, multi-scale delayed accumulation scheme that constrains how fast the effective pre-conditioner can change. The theoretical analysis covers both online convex and stochastic non-convex settings, with the main goal being convergence across the full adaptivity spectrum. The novelty is less about a new moment estimator and more about elevating pre-conditioner sensitivity itself into the primary optimizer design axis.
summary_en.experiments: From the available full-text content, experiments span image classification, language, and generative modeling, and the authors claim consistent gains over strong baselines across tasks and architectures. However, the visible excerpt does not include the detailed tables that would matter most for pretraining readers: model sizes, token budgets, exact language modeling metrics, and the gap to AdamW under matched tuning. What does seem central is that the paper studies performance as a function of continuous adaptivity, rather than only comparing named optimizers, and that it compares IDU against AMSGrad-style stabilization under extreme gamma values. Those two evaluations are important because they test the paper’s actual thesis: fixed adaptivity is limiting, and broader adaptivity requires a new convergence mechanism. If the full paper includes large-scale LM training curves, that section deserves attention; otherwise the work is better read as an optimizer design framework than as a drop-in pretraining recipe.
summary_en.reading_guide: A good skim should focus on three parts. First, read the adaptivity definition in Section 2.2 carefully; that is where the paper either earns its unifying claim or collapses into a re-labeling exercise. Second, inspect the update rule in Section 3.1 to see exactly how gamma enters the pre-conditioner and what negative versus super-unit adaptivity means operationally. Third, read the IDU section and the convergence proofs with one practical question in mind: is this stabilization genuinely needed, or is it a dressed-up variant of existing max-tracking ideas. In the experiments, prioritize plots of performance versus gamma, sensitivity to learning rate and weight decay, and whether the preferred adaptivity shifts across tasks or training phases. A useful first pass should take about 30 to 45 minutes.

recommendation.zh: 先看 optimizer 定义和噪声实验；若只停留在小模型理论，不能直接改预训练默认 AdamW。
recommendation.en: Check the optimizer definition and noise experiments first; without large-model evidence, it should not displace AdamW in pretraining.

paper.title: Learning Rate Engineering: From Coarse Single Parameter to Layered Evolution
paper.abstract: Learning rate scheduling has evolved from the single global fixed rate of early SGD to sophisticated layer-wise adaptive strategies. We systematize this evolution into five generations: (Gen1) global fixed learning rates, (Gen2) global scheduling, (Gen3) parameter-level adaptation, (Gen4) layer-level differentiation, and (Gen5) joint layer-time scheduling. summary.core_problem: 系统化梳理学习率调度从全局固定值到分层、随时间演化策略的发展，并提出一个结合层级差异和训练阶段的优化框架。
summary.importance: 这是优化器和学习率工程综述加方法论文。贡献在于 taxonomy 和 DALS 组合式优化框架；但摘要主要面向迁移学习，不是大规模 LLM 预训练设置，因此对基座训练的直接可迁移性有限。
summary.technical_approach: 论文把学习率策略分为五代：全局固定、全局 schedule、参数级自适应、层级差异化、层-时间联合调度。DALS 结合 phase-adaptive cosine scheduling、depth-aware Grokfast gradient filtering 和 LARS-style trust ratio，希望同时处理低层保留通用知识、高层快速适配任务的冲突。
summary.experiments: 摘要称比较了 18 种策略和 3 个 DALS 变体，但未给出具体模型、数据集、规模和提升幅度。需要核验实验是否覆盖 Transformer/LLM 训练，还是主要在中小规模迁移学习任务上成立。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper organizes the evolution of learning-rate scheduling from a single global value to layer-wise and time-varying strategies, and proposes an optimizer framework combining both dimensions.
summary_en.importance: This is an optimizer and learning-rate-engineering paper with a taxonomy plus a combined method called DALS. The abstract is mainly framed around transfer learning rather than large-scale LLM pretraining, so its direct transferability to base-model training is uncertain.
summary_en.technical_approach: The paper classifies learning-rate methods into five generations: global fixed rates, global schedules, parameter-level adaptation, layer-level differentiation, and joint layer-time scheduling. DALS combines phase-adaptive cosine scheduling, depth-aware Grokfast gradient filtering, and LARS-style trust ratios to balance preserving lower-layer knowledge with adapting higher layers.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract reports benchmarking 18 strategies and three DALS variants, but does not specify the model families, datasets, scale, or numerical gains. It is important to check whether the experiments include Transformer or LLM training rather than only small transfer-learning tasks.

recommendation.zh: 作为 LR taxonomy 可快速扫；DALS 若没在 Transformer 预训练规模验证，就只能当 fine-tuning trick 备查。
recommendation.en: Skim it as an LR taxonomy; unless DALS is tested at Transformer pretraining scale, treat it as a fine-tuning trick reference.

paper.title: DeepSeek-V4: Towards Highly Efficient Million-Token Context Intelligence
paper.abstract:
We present a preview version of DeepSeek-V4 series, including two strong Mixture-of- Experts (MoE) language models — DeepSeek-V4-Pro with 1.6T parameters (49B activated) and DeepSeek-V4-Flash with 284B parameters (13B activated) — both supporting a context length of one million tokens. DeepSeek-V4 series incorporate several key upgrades in architecture and op- timization: (1) a hybrid attention architecture that combines Compressed Sparse Attention (CSA) and Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA) to improve long-context efficiency; (2) Manifold- Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) that enhance conventional residual connections; (3) and the Muon optimizer for faster convergence and greater training stability. We pre-train both models on more than 32T diverse and high-quality tokens, followed by a comprehensive post-training pipeline that unlocks and further enhances their capabilities. DeepSeek-V4-Pro- Max, the maximum reasoning effort mode of DeepSeek-V4-Pro, redefines the state-of-the-art for open models, outperforming its predecessors in core tasks. Meanwhile, DeepSeek-V4 series are highly efficient in long-context scenarios. In the one-million-token context setting, DeepSeek- V4-Pro requires only 27% of single-token inference FLOPs and 10% of KV cache compared with DeepSeek-V3.2. This enables us to routinely support one-million-token contexts, thereby making long-horizon tasks and further test-time scaling more feasible. The model checkpoints are available at https://huggingfa

1. Introduction
The emergence of reasoning models (DeepSeek-AI, 2025; OpenAI, 2024c) has established a
new paradigm of test-time scaling, driving substantial performance gains for Large Language
Models (LLMs). However, this scaling paradigm is fundamentally constrained by the quadratic
computational complexity of the vanilla attention mechanism (Vaswani et al., 2017), which
creates a prohibitive bottleneck for ultra-long contexts and reasoning processes. Concurrently,
the emergence of long-horizon scenarios and tasks — from complex agentic workflows to
massive cross-document analysis — has also made efficient support for ultra-long contexts
critical for future progress. While recent open-source efforts (Bai et al., 2025a; DeepSeek-AI,
2024; MiniMax, 2025; Qwen, 2025) have advanced general capabilities, this core architectural
inefficiency in handling ultra-long sequences remains a key impediment, limiting further gains
from test-time scaling and hindering further exploration into long-horizon scenarios and tasks.
In order to break the efficiency barrier in ultra-long contexts, we develop the DeepSeek-V4
series, including the preview versions of DeepSeek-V4-Pro with 1.6T parameters (49B activated)
and DeepSeek-V4-Flash with 284B parameters (13B activated). Through architectural innova-
tions, DeepSeek-V4 series achieve a dramatic leap in computational efficiency for processing
ultra-long sequences. This breakthrough enables efficient support for a context length of one
million tokens, ushering in a new era of million-length contexts for next-generation LLMs. We
believe our capability to efficiently handle ultra-long sequences unlocks the next frontier of
test-time scaling, paves the way for deeper research into long-horizon tasks, and establishes a
necessary foundation for exploring future paradigms like online learning.
Compared with the DeepSeek-V3 architecture (DeepSeek-AI, 2024), DeepSeek-V4 series
retain the DeepSeekMoE framework (Dai et al., 2024) and Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) strategy,
while introducing several key innovations in architecture and optimization. To enhance long-
context efficiency, we design a hybrid attention mechanism combining Compressed Sparse
Attention (CSA) and Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA). CSA compresses the KV caches
along the sequence dimension and then performs DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) (DeepSeek-
AI, 2025), whereas HCA applies more aggressive compression to the KV caches but keeps
dense attention. To strengthen modeling capability, we incorporate Manifold-Constrained
Hyper-Connections (mHC) (Xie et al., 2026) that upgrade conventional residual connections.
Additionally, we introduce the Muon (Jordan et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025) optimizer to the
training of DeepSeek-V4 series, leading to faster convergence and improved training stability.
To enable efficient training and inference for DeepSeek-V4 series as well as productive de-
velopment, we introduce several infrastructure optimizations. First, we design and implement
a single fused kernel for MoE modules that fully overlaps computation, communication, and
memory access. Second, we employ TileLang (Wang et al., 2026), a Domain-Specific Language
(DSL) to balance development productivity and runtime efficiency. Third, we provide efficient
batch-invariant and deterministic kernel libraries to ensure bitwise reproducibility across train-
ing and inference. Fourth, we incorporate FP4 quantization-aware training for MoE expert
weights and the indexer QK path to reduce memory and computation. Fifth, for the training
framework, we extend the autograd framework with tensor-level checkpointing for fine-grained
recomputation control; and we enhance training efficiency with a hybrid ZeRO strategy for the
Muon optimizer, cost-effective mHC implementations via recomputation and fused kernels, and
two-stage contextual parallelism to manage compressed attention. Finally, for the inference
framework, we design a heterogeneous KV cache structure with on-disk storage strategies to
enable efficient shared-prefix reuse.
4

By employing hybrid CSA and HCA, along with precision optimizations on computation
and storage, DeepSeek-V4 series achieve significantly lower inference FLOPs and a substantially
reduced KV cache size compared with DeepSeek-V3.2, especially in long-context settings. The
right part of Figure 1 demonstrates the estimated single-token inference FLOPs and accumulated
KV cache size of DeepSeek-V3.2 and DeepSeek-V4 series. In the scenario of 1M-token context,
even DeepSeek-V4-Pro, which has a larger number of activated parameters, attains only 27%
of the single-token FLOPs (measured in equivalent FP8 FLOPs) and 10% of the KV cache
size relative to DeepSeek-V3.2. Furthermore, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, with its smaller number of

only 10% of the single-token FLOPs and 7% of the KV cache size compared with DeepSeek-V3.2.
Additionally, for DeepSeek-V4 series, the routed expert parameters utilize FP4 precision. While
the peak FLOPs for FP4 × FP8 operations are currently the same as FP8 × FP8 on existing
hardware, they can theoretically be implemented to be 1/3 more efficient on future hardware,
which will further enhance the efficiency of DeepSeek-V4 series.
During pre-training, we train DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 32T tokens and DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 33T
tokens, respectively. After pre-training, these two models can natively and efficiently support
1M-length contexts. In our internal evaluations, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base already surpasses
DeepSeek-V3.2-Base across a majority of benchmarks with its more parameter-efficient design.
DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base further extends this advantage to set a new performance standard among
DeepSeek foundation models, achieving comprehensive superiority across reasoning, coding,
long-context, and world knowledge tasks.
The post-training pipeline of DeepSeek-V4 series features a two-stage paradigm: the inde-
pendent cultivation of domain-specific experts, followed by unified model consolidation via
on-policy distillation (Lu and Lab, 2025). Initially, for each target domain — such as mathematics,
coding, agent, and instruction following — a separate expert model is trained independently.
The base model first undergoes Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on high-quality, domain-specific
data to establish foundational capabilities. Subsequently, Reinforcement Learning (RL) is ap-
plied using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) (DeepSeek-AI, 2025), which further
optimizes the model for domain-aligned behaviors guided by reward models tailored to specific
success criteria. This phase yields a diverse set of specialized experts, each excelling in its
respective field. Finally, to integrate these distinct proficiencies, a single unified model is trained
through on-policy distillation, wherein the unified model acts as the student learning to optimize
the reverse KL loss with teacher models.

1. Introduction
The emergence of reasoning models (DeepSeek-AI, 2025; OpenAI, 2024c) has established a
new paradigm of test-time scaling, driving substantial performance gains for Large Language
Models (LLMs). However, this scaling paradigm is fundamentally constrained by the quadratic
computational complexity of the vanilla attention mechanism (Vaswani et al., 2017), which
creates a prohibitive bottleneck for ultra-long contexts and reasoning processes. Concurrently,
the emergence of long-horizon scenarios and tasks — from complex agentic workflows to
massive cross-document analysis — has also made efficient support for ultra-long contexts
critical for future progress. While recent open-source efforts (Bai et al., 2025a; DeepSeek-AI,
2024; MiniMax, 2025; Qwen, 2025) have advanced general capabilities, this core architectural
inefficiency in handling ultra-long sequences remains a key impediment, limiting further gains
from test-time scaling and hindering further exploration into long-horizon scenarios and tasks.
In order to break the efficiency barrier in ultra-long contexts, we develop the DeepSeek-V4
series, including the preview versions of DeepSeek-V4-Pro with 1.6T parameters (49B activated)
and DeepSeek-V4-Flash with 284B parameters (13B activated). Through architectural innova-
tions, DeepSeek-V4 series achieve a dramatic leap in computational efficiency for processing
ultra-long sequences. This breakthrough enables efficient support for a context length of one
million tokens, ushering in a new era of million-length contexts for next-generation LLMs. We
believe our capability to efficiently handle ultra-long sequences unlocks the next frontier of
test-time scaling, paves the way for deeper research into long-horizon tasks, and establishes a
necessary foundation for exploring future paradigms like online learning.
Compared with the DeepSeek-V3 architecture (DeepSeek-AI, 2024), DeepSeek-V4 series
retain the DeepSeekMoE framework (Dai et al., 2024) and Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) strategy,
while introducing several key innovations in architecture and optimization. To enhance long-
context efficiency, we design a hybrid attention mechanism combining Compressed Sparse
Attention (CSA) and Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA). CSA compresses the KV caches
along the sequence dimension and then performs DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) (DeepSeek-
AI, 2025), whereas HCA applies more aggressive compression to the KV caches but keeps
dense attention. To strengthen modeling capability, we incorporate Manifold-Constrained
Hyper-Connections (mHC) (Xie et al., 2026) that upgrade conventional residual connections.
Additionally, we introduce the Muon (Jordan et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025) optimizer to the
training of DeepSeek-V4 series, leading to faster convergence and improved training stability.
To enable efficient training and inference for DeepSeek-V4 series as well as productive de-
velopment, we introduce several infrastructure optimizations. First, we design and implement
a single fused kernel for MoE modules that fully overlaps computation, communication, and
memory access. Second, we employ TileLang (Wang et al., 2026), a Domain-Specific Language
(DSL) to balance development productivity and runtime efficiency. Third, we provide efficient
batch-invariant and deterministic kernel libraries to ensure bitwise reproducibility across train-
ing and inference. Fourth, we incorporate FP4 quantization-aware training for MoE expert
weights and the indexer QK path to reduce memory and computation. Fifth, for the training
framework, we extend the autograd framework with tensor-level checkpointing for fine-grained
recomputation control; and we enhance training efficiency with a hybrid ZeRO strategy for the
Muon optimizer, cost-effective mHC implementations via recomputation and fused kernels, and
two-stage contextual parallelism to manage compressed attention. Finally, for the inference
framework, we design a heterogeneous KV cache structure with on-disk storage strategies to
enable efficient shared-prefix reuse.

2. Architecture
Overall, DeepSeek-V4 series retain the Transformer (Vaswani et al., 2017) architecture and Multi-
Token Prediction (MTP) modules (DeepSeek-AI, 2024; Gloeckle et al., 2024), while introducing
several key upgrades over DeepSeek-V3: (1) firstly, we introduce the Manifold-Constrained
Hyper-Connections (mHC) (Xie et al., 2026) to strengthen conventional residual connections;
6

(2) secondly, we design a hybrid attention architecture, which greatly improves long-context
efficiency through Compressed Sparse Attention and Heavily Compressed Attention. (3) thirdly,
we employ Muon (Jordan et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025) as the optimizer. For the Mixture-of-
Experts (MoE) components, we still adopt the DeepSeekMoE (Dai et al., 2024) architecture, with
only minor adjustments from DeepSeek-V3. The Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) (DeepSeek-AI,
2024; Gloeckle et al., 2024; Li et al., 2024; Qi et al., 2020) configuration remains identical to
that of DeepSeek-V3. All other unspecified details follow the settings established in DeepSeek-
V3 (DeepSeek-AI, 2024). Figure 2 illustrates the overall architecture of DeepSeek-V4, and the
details are described below.
2.1. Designs Inherited from DeepSeek-V3
Mixture-of-Experts.
As previous DeepSeek-series models (DeepSeek-AI, 2024; DeepSeek-AI,
2024), DeepSeek-V4 series also adopt the DeepSeekMoE paradigm (Dai et al., 2024) for Feed-
Forward Networks (FFNs), which sets fine-grained routed experts and shared experts. Different
from DeepSeek-V3, we change the activation function that computes the affinity scores from
Sigmoid(·) into Sqrt(Softplus(·)). For load balancing, we also employ the auxiliary-loss-free
strategy (DeepSeek-AI, 2024; Wang et al., 2024a), augmented by a slight sequence-wise balance
loss that prevents extreme imbalance within individual sequences. For DeepSeek-V4, we remove
the constraint on the number of routing target nodes, and carefully redesign the parallelism
strategy to maintain training efficiency. Furthermore, compared with DeepSeek-V3, we replace
the dense FFN layers in the initial several Transformer blocks with MoE layers that employ
Hash routing (Roller et al., 2021). The Hash routing strategy determines the target experts of
each token according to a predefined hash function with regard to the input token ID.
Multi-Token Prediction.
As DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-V4 series also set MTP modules and
objectives. Given that the MTP strategy has been validated in DeepSeek-V3, we adopt the same
strategy for DeepSeek-V4 series without modification.
2.2. Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections
As shown in Figure 2, DeepSeek-V4 series incorporate Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections
(mHC) (Xie et al., 2026) to strengthen the conventional residual connections between adjacent

idea of mHC is to constrain the residual mapping onto a specific manifold, and thus enhance the
stability of signal propagation across layers while preserving model expressivity. This subsection
briefly introduces the standard HC and describes how we design mHC for stable training.

(1)

2.3. Hybrid Attention with CSA and HCA
As the context length reaches extreme scales, the attention mechanism emerges as the dominant
computational bottleneck in a model. For DeepSeek-V4, we design two efficient attention
architectures — Compressed Sparse Attention (CSA) and Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA)
— and employ their interleaved hybrid configuration, which substantially reduces the compu-
tational cost of attention in long-text scenarios. CSA integrates both compression and sparse
attention strategies: it first compresses the Key-Value (KV) cache of every 𝑚tokens into one
entry, and then applies DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) (DeepSeek-AI, 2025) where each query
token attends to only 𝑘compressed KV entries. HCA aims for extreme compression by consol-
idating the KV cache of every 𝑚′ (≫𝑚) tokens into a single entry. The hybrid architecture of
CSA and HCA remarkably improves the long-context efficiency of DeepSeek-V4 series, making
one-million-token context feasible in practice. This subsection describes the core techniques
of our hybrid attention architecture, and we also provide an open-source implementation1 to
specify more details unambiguously.
