summary.core_problem: 这篇技术报告讨论的是：在超长上下文已经从展示能力走向日常可用之后，如何把百万 token 上下文做成一个训练、推理、成本三者都能成立的基座模型方案。核心关注点不是单点长上下文技巧，而是 MoE 架构、注意力压缩、残差连接改造、优化器与后训练如何一起支撑 1M context。
summary.key_insights: 最值得记住的是三件事。第一，DeepSeek 把长上下文问题明确当成系统级预训练问题来做，而不是只靠 RoPE 外推或推理时工程补丁；CSA+HCA 的混合注意力直接瞄准单 token FLOPs 和 KV cache 两个主要瓶颈，报告里给出在 1M context 下相对 V3.2 约 27% FLOPs、10% KV cache 的量级。第二，mHC 和 Muon 被放在与注意力同等重要的位置，说明他们判断百万上下文的可用性不只是 inference efficiency，还取决于深层网络训练稳定性和收敛速度。第三，32T token 预训练加完整 post-training pipeline，配合 reasoning mode，表明长上下文能力已经被当成通用能力底座，而不是单独拉一条长文本 benchmark 曲线。
summary.limits: 当前信息主要来自预览版技术报告，很多关键细节还不够展开，例如 CSA/HCA 的精确机制、不同长度区间的质量-成本折中、mHC 相对标准残差的独立增益、Muon 在这一规模下的稳定性边界，以及 1M context 是否真正转化为稳定的长程任务收益。基准图里也混合了预训练、后训练和推理 effort 的共同效果，暂时不容易拆出各模块的因果贡献。

summary_en.core_problem: This report asks a practical pretraining question: how do you make million-token context a routine capability rather than a demo feature? The focus is not just context extension, but a full-stack recipe spanning MoE design, compressed attention, residual-path changes, optimizer choice, and post-training.
summary_en.key_insights: Three points matter. First, DeepSeek treats long context as a model-design problem, not merely a positional extrapolation trick. The CSA+HCA hybrid attention is aimed directly at the two real inference bottlenecks at 1M length: per-token FLOPs and KV cache, with reported reductions to roughly 27% FLOPs and 10% KV cache versus V3.2. Second, mHC and Muon are presented as core ingredients, which suggests the team sees long-context viability as tightly coupled to optimization stability and deep-network training dynamics, not just serving efficiency. Third, the combination of 32T-token pretraining and a substantial post-training stack indicates that long-context competence is being folded into the general-purpose model backbone rather than treated as a narrow benchmark specialization.
summary_en.limits: It is still a preview report, so several important pieces remain underspecified: the exact CSA/HCA mechanics, quality-cost tradeoffs across different context ranges, the standalone contribution of mHC over standard residual designs, and the stability envelope of Muon at this scale. The headline benchmark gains also mix pretraining, post-training, and reasoning-effort effects, so the causal contribution of each component is not yet cleanly isolated.

recommendation.zh: DeepSeek 把百万上下文当作系统级预训练问题来答，而不是推理期 hack：CSA+HCA 混合注意力直接压 FLOPs 和 KV cache，配合 mHC、Muon 与 32T token 预训练，是目前开源侧看长上下文基座最完整的一份作业，值得精读对照 V3.2 看每一项的增量。
recommendation.en: DeepSeek frames the million-token context as a pretraining-systems problem rather than an inference-time hack. The CSA+HCA hybrid attention attacks FLOPs and KV-cache directly, paired with mHC, Muon, and 32T-token pretraining — the most complete open-side blueprint for a long-context base model today, worth reading closely against V3.2 to isolate per-component gains.

paper.title: Convergent Evolution: How Different Language Models Learn Similar Number Representations
paper.abstract: Language models trained on natural text learn to represent numbers using periodic features with dominant periods at $T=2, 5, 10$. In this paper, we identify a two-tiered hierarchy of these features: while Transformers, Linear RNNs, LSTMs, and classical word embeddings trained in different ways all learn features that have period-$T$ spikes in the Fourier domain, only some learn geometrically separable features that can be used to linearly classify a number mod-$T$. To explain this incongruity, w

summary.core_problem: 很多工作把“数字 token embedding 出现 T=2/5/10 的傅里叶尖峰”解读为模型学到了可用的数概念结构。但全文给出的核心问题更尖锐：为什么几乎所有系统（Transformer、线性 RNN、LSTM、传统词向量，甚至仅语料频次分布）都会出现相似的频谱尖峰（spectral convergence），但只有一部分系统的数字 embedding 才能把 n mod T 线性可分（geometric convergence）？也就是：频谱尖峰到底来自数据/分词的统计偏置，还是来自模型学到的可计算结构；以及什么条件决定“尖峰”能否转化为可线性解码的模结构。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的影响主要在“机制归因”和“数据-分词-优化-架构耦合”两点。第一，它把一个常见的机制解释（数字 embedding 的周期结构=模型学会了模运算）拆成两层，并证明“有尖峰”并不等价于“可线性读出模类”，避免把数据诱导的统计结构误当成模型能力。第二，它用受控训练把几类因素（数据中的数字共现与跨数字交互、上下文长度、架构、优化器、tokenizer）逐一剥离，给出更工程化的结论：哪些信号会让几何可分出现，哪些只会保留频谱尖峰。这类结论对做数据配比、tokenizer 设计、以及解释训练动态（为什么某些结构在某些架构里“长出来”）都直接有用。
summary.technical_approach:
方法分三块。
1) 现象与度量：固定研究对象为 0..999 的数字 token embedding e(n)。沿 token index 做 DFT，观察功率谱在 1/T 处的尖峰（T=2/5/10）。同时用线性 probe（T 类 logistic regression）预测 n mod T，作为“几何可分/可线性读出”的 operational 定义。
2) 理论区分：给出结论“傅里叶域稀疏（有尖峰）是 mod-T 可分的必要条件，但不是充分条件”。直观上，尖峰只说明 embedding 在 token 序上有周期分量；但要线性分开 residue class，需要这些周期分量在几何上形成可被一个线性分类器稳定切分的簇/方向结构。论文用定理（Theorem 1）形式化了这种不充分性，并解释了为何两个系统可以有几乎相同的频谱，却 probe 准确率天差地别。
3) 结构归因式的受控实验：在相同规模（文中强调 300M 参数）与相同训练数据的条件下，系统性改变单一因素来观察“尖峰是否仍在”与“probe 是否掉到随机”。数据侧做逐步去除：削弱文本-数字共现、削弱跨数字交互、缩短上下文等；架构侧对比 Transformer、线性 RNN、LSTM；优化侧比较不同优化器在相同架构下对几何可分的影响；tokenizer 侧用“从零训练加法”任务对比单 token vs 多 token 表示数字，展示多 token 加法会强迫出现模子问题（例如按位/按块的模 1000 结构），从而更稳定地产生圆形/周期表示，而单 token 加法存在多种可行策略，表示会更依赖优化路径（optimizer-dependent）。
summary.experiments:
全文实验的关键不是单一 SOTA 数字，而是“同频谱、不同可分性”的对照与消融趋势。
- 广泛性：在多种已发布模型与非 Transformer 系统、以及 GloVe/FastText 中都观察到 T=2/5/10 的尖峰；甚至仅统计训练语料中数字 token 的频次分布也出现相似频谱（用来支持“数据/分词诱导”的解释）。
- 两层收敛：spectral convergence 几乎处处存在；geometric convergence 只在部分系统出现。文中给出强对照：Transformer 与线性 RNN（在约 10B token 训练设置下）能把 mod-T 线性 probe 做到很高，而 LSTM 在相同数据下即使尖峰更显著，probe 仍接近随机水平。
- 数据消融：逐步移除文本-数字共现、跨数字交互、或缩短上下文长度，会显著降低 mod-T probe；但傅里叶尖峰在这些条件下仍然顽固存在，支持“尖峰更像数据统计投影，几何可分需要额外语义/组合信号”的判断。
- 架构/优化：架构对几何可分是决定性的（Transformer/线性 RNN vs LSTM）；优化器在某些设置下会改变是否学到可分结构，但不会改变尖峰出现这一事实。
- tokenizer 与任务约束：在从零训练的加法任务里，多 token 表示数字会迫使模型解决按位/按块的模子问题，从而更稳定地产生周期/圆形结构；单 token 表示数字时，模型可能走不同捷径，导致表示对优化路径更敏感、结果更不稳定。
（注：你给的全文片段未包含所有表格具体数值；上述以论文主线结论与对照关系为主，数字细节应以正文图表为准。）
summary.reading_guide:
精读建议按“先建立区分，再看归因”走。
- 先看问题设定与度量：Problem Setup 里 DFT 的定义、Fourier spike 的 operational 定义、以及 mod-T 线性 probe 的设置。这里决定了后面所有结论的可比性。
- 重点看理论段落（含 Theorem 1）：抓住“必要不充分”的条件到底卡在哪里。建议对照论文给出的反例/解释：同样的频谱稀疏如何对应到不同的几何布局。
- 重点看三组受控实验：
  1) 数据信号逐步移除的消融（最能说明‘尖峰不等于能力’）；
  2) 架构对照（Transformer/线性 RNN/LSTM 在同数据同规模下的 probe 差异）；
  3) tokenizer + 加法任务（多 token 强约束如何“逼出”模结构）。
- 如果时间有限：只看 Figure 1/2（广泛性与语料频谱）、以及架构对照与数据消融对应的主图，就能把论文的核心论证链条串起来。

summary_en.core_problem: Prior work often treats Fourier spikes (dominant periods around T=2/5/10) in number token embeddings as evidence that LMs learn structured numerical representations. The paper’s actual core question is sharper: why do Fourier spikes ("spectral convergence") appear almost universally—across Transformers, linear RNNs, LSTMs, classical word embeddings, and even the raw corpus frequency of number tokens—while only some systems yield embeddings where residue classes n mod T are linearly decodable ("geometric convergence")? In other words, what part is a data/tokenization-induced statistical artifact, and what part reflects a learned, functionally usable modular structure—and which training conditions control the transition from spectral to geometric convergence?
summary_en.importance: The contribution is mainly methodological and interpretability-relevant for pretraining research. (1) It cleanly separates two phenomena that are frequently conflated: periodic spectra vs linearly usable modular codes. This prevents over-interpreting a ubiquitous spectral signature as a learned arithmetic capability. (2) It runs controlled “structure attribution” experiments that isolate how data signals (text–number co-occurrence, cross-number interactions, context length), architecture choice, optimizer, and tokenizer jointly determine whether modular structure becomes linearly accessible. These findings are directly actionable for data design, tokenizer decisions, and for understanding training dynamics where certain representations reliably emerge in some architectures but not others.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The approach has three pillars.
1) Metrics and setup: focus on embeddings e(n) for number tokens n in 0..999 (aligned with common tokenizers where these are single tokens). Compute a DFT along the token index and measure power at frequencies 1/T to identify spikes. Separately, train a linear probe (T-way logistic regression) to predict n mod T from e(n), operationalizing “geometric separability.”
2) Theory: prove that Fourier-domain sparsity/spikes are necessary but not sufficient for mod-T linear separability (Theorem 1). Intuitively, a periodic component in the sequence of embeddings does not guarantee that residue classes form linearly separable clusters; two systems can share near-identical spectra yet differ drastically in the geometry relevant to linear decoding.
3) Controlled attribution experiments: train ~300M-parameter models on matched data while perturbing one factor at a time. Data-side perturbations progressively remove (i) text–number co-occurrence, (ii) cross-number interaction signals, and (iii) long-context dependencies. Architecture comparisons include Transformers vs linear RNNs vs LSTMs under identical data. Optimizer comparisons test whether optimization path affects geometric convergence even when spectral convergence is stable. Tokenizer effects are probed via training-from-scratch addition tasks: multi-token numbers force modular subproblems (e.g., digit/block-wise modulo constraints), making circular/periodic representations more stable; single-token numbers admit multiple solution strategies, making learned representations more optimizer-dependent.
summary_en.experiments:
The experimental story is built around contrasts and ablations rather than a single headline benchmark.
- Universality: T=2/5/10 spikes are observed across many released LMs and non-Transformer sequence models, plus GloVe/FastText; strikingly, the corpus-level frequency distribution of number tokens already exhibits a similar periodic spectrum.
- Two-tier outcome: spectral convergence is near-universal; geometric convergence is not. A key controlled contrast: Transformers and linear RNNs (in large-token training settings) yield high mod-T probe accuracy, while LSTMs trained on the same data can show even stronger spikes yet remain near chance on mod-T probing.
- Data ablations: removing co-occurrence, cross-number interactions, or reducing context length degrades mod-T probe accuracy substantially, while Fourier spikes persist—supporting the claim that spikes are largely data/tokenization-driven, whereas linear decodability requires additional structured signals.
- Architecture/optimizer: architecture is decisive for geometric convergence; optimizer can affect whether separable structure emerges in some settings, but does not eliminate the spectral spikes.
- Tokenizer/task constraint: in addition-from-scratch, multi-token number representations more reliably induce modular/circular features due to forced modulo subproblems; single-token setups allow alternative shortcuts, leading to higher variance and optimizer dependence.
(Note: the provided full-text excerpt does not include all numeric tables; exact probe accuracies and training details should be taken from the corresponding figures/tables in the paper.)
summary_en.reading_guide:
Read it in the order that mirrors the argument.
- Start with the formal setup: how the DFT is computed over e(n), what counts as a Fourier spike, and how the mod-T linear probe is defined.
- Then read the theorem section carefully (Theorem 1): the paper’s main conceptual move is the “necessary but not sufficient” separation; understanding the geometric failure modes is the point.
- Spend most time on the controlled experiments:
  (i) data-signal removal ablations (best evidence that spikes ≠ usable structure),
  (ii) architecture-matched comparisons (Transformer/linear RNN vs LSTM),
  (iii) tokenizer + addition task (why multi-token constraints reliably produce modular codes).
- If time is tight: focus on the early figures showing universality (including corpus frequency spectrum) and the architecture/ablation figures that juxtapose stable spikes with collapsing probe accuracy.

recommendation.zh: 这篇会改你看 probing 结果的方式：看到周期峰值别急着说模型学会了数论结构，先区分 Fourier 稀疏和几何可分；建议直接复现它的 tokenizer/optimizer ablation。
recommendation.en: This should change how you read probing results: a Fourier spike does not mean the model learned modular structure; separate spectral sparsity from geometric separability and replicate the tokenizer/optimizer ablations.

paper.title: Muon$^2$: Boosting Muon via Adaptive Second-Moment Preconditioning

summary.core_problem: Muon 通过 Newton–Schulz(NS) 迭代近似动量矩阵的极分解/正交因子来改善大模型预训练的优化动力学，但每步需要多次 NS 迭代，带来显著计算与分布式通信开销；核心问题是：能否在减少正交化迭代负担的同时，保持甚至提升 Muon 的训练效果？
summary.importance: 该问题直接关系到“预训练吞吐/成本”与“收敛质量/稳定性”的共同最优：Muon 的优势来自矩阵结构更新与抑制 rank collapse，但其 NS 迭代是系统瓶颈之一。若能用更少迭代达到“足够好”的方向更新，就能在大规模分布式训练中同时获得更高效率与更强性能。
summary.technical_approach:
【must_read：详细技术分析】
1) 关键改动（Muon2）：在进入正交化之前，对动量矩阵做 Adam/AdamW 风格的逐元素二阶矩自适应缩放（second-moment preconditioning）。流程是：先用一阶动量得到 M_t，再维护二阶矩 V_t（对梯度或动量的逐元素平方做 EMA），形成预条件后的动量 \tilde{M}_t = M_t ⊘ (\sqrt{V_t}+\epsilon)，再对 \tilde{M}_t 做 K 步 NS 迭代得到近似正交因子 Q_t，最后用带 \sqrt{m/n} 的学习率缩放更新参数。
2) 核心洞见：Muon 中极分解近似的“难点”不在于必须追求严格正交（论文指出 Muon 原本就允许较大误差，例如把奇异值粗略压到 [1-ε,1+ε] 且 ε 可到 ~0.3 仍有效），而在于输入到 NS 的矩阵（动量矩阵）往往谱条件数差、奇异值分布不理想，导致 NS 收敛慢、需要更多迭代。Muon2 的逐元素二阶矩缩放在经验上显著改善奇异值谱（更“平坦/均衡”），从而：
- 加速 NS 迭代达到“实践上足够”的正交化质量；
- 提升最终更新方向与“真实正交化更新”的对齐（directional alignment），即便不追求严格正交度指标。
3) 评价指标视角的转变：论文强调仅用 \|Q^TQ-I\| 这类“正交性误差”不足以解释优化效果，应更关注更新方向与极分解目标的对齐程度，以及在有限迭代下对训练损失/稳定性的实际贡献。
4) Muon2-F：为降低保存完整二阶矩的显存/内存开销，引入因子化（factorized）二阶矩预条件器，在尽量保留 Muon2 性能增益的同时显著减小内存占用，适配大模型预训练的工程约束。

【skim：方法概述】在 Muon 的“动量→NS 正交化→更新”链路中，插入一个 Adam 式二阶矩逐元素缩放作为预条件，使 NS 更快收敛，因此可以用更少 NS 步数获得更好/不降的训练效果；另提供因子化二阶矩版本以省内存。
summary.experiments: 在 GPT-Small/Base/Large 以及 LLaMA（约 60M–1B）预训练实验中，Muon2 与 Muon2-F 相比 Muon/其他基线在整体性能上更优，并且在保持或提升效果的同时，将每步所需 NS 迭代数减少约 40%（从而降低计算与通信开销）。论文还通过谱分布/条件数与方向对齐等分析，实证支持“二阶矩预条件改善谱→NS 更快→效果更好”的因果链条。
summary.reading_guide:
【must_read：精读建议】
- Introduction：抓住论文动机：Muon 的系统瓶颈是 NS 迭代；作者主张“足够的近似正交化”而非严格正交。
- The Muon2 Optimizer（算法/公式段落，含 Eq.(4) 与 Algorithm 1）：逐行对照 Muon 与 Muon2 的唯一区别——二阶矩缩放插入位置；理解 \tilde{M}_t 的定义与学习率 \sqrt{m/n} 缩放的作用。
- 理论/分析部分（关于谱条件数、奇异值分布、directional alignment、以及为何正交性误差不足）：这是论文创新论证的核心，建议重点看作者如何把“优化有效性”从正交度指标转向“方向对齐+有限迭代实用性”。
- Muon2-F：重点看因子化二阶矩如何构造、节省多少内存、以及与全量二阶矩的性能差距。
- 实验部分：优先看（1）NS 迭代数减少与吞吐收益；（2）不同模型规模上的一致性；（3）谱/奇异值可视化或对齐度曲线（若有图表，通常最能支撑核心主张）。

【skim：泛读建议】
- 只读 Introduction + Algorithm 1/关键公式（Muon2 的插入点）+ 主结果表（不同模型规模）+ “NS 迭代数/效率”对比图；若关心落地，再扫一遍 Muon2-F 的内存对比与性能表。
summary.authors_note: 作者的立场是“工程上足够好的正交化”比“数学上严格正交”更关键：Muon 的收益来自更新方向与谱形态的改善，而 NS 迭代只是实现手段。Muon2 用 Adam 式二阶矩预条件先把输入矩阵变得更好正交化，从而用更少迭代达到更好的方向更新与最终性能；Muon2-F 则补齐大规模训练的内存约束。

summary_en.core_problem: Muon improves large-scale pre-training by orthogonalizing matrix-shaped updates via Newton–Schulz (NS) iterations (polar factor approximation), but it typically requires multiple NS steps per optimizer step, creating non-trivial compute and distributed communication overhead. The problem is whether we can reduce the orthogonalization burden while preserving or improving Muon’s training quality.
summary_en.importance: This directly impacts both system efficiency (throughput/cost) and optimization quality (stability/final loss). Muon’s gains come from exploiting matrix structure and mitigating rank collapse, yet NS iterations can become a bottleneck at scale. Achieving a “good-enough” orthogonalized direction with fewer iterations can yield meaningful end-to-end pre-training speedups without sacrificing performance.
summary_en.technical_approach:
[must_read: detailed technical analysis]
1) Main change (Muon2): apply Adam-style adaptive second-moment, element-wise scaling to the momentum matrix before the NS-based orthogonalization. Concretely: form momentum M_t, maintain a second-moment accumulator V_t (EMA of squared signals), compute a preconditioned momentum \tilde{M}_t = M_t / (\sqrt{V_t}+\epsilon) element-wise, then run K NS iterations on \tilde{M}_t to obtain an approximate polar/orthogonal factor Q_t, and update parameters with an additional \sqrt{m/n} learning-rate scaling.
2) Key insight: the practical difficulty in Muon’s polar approximation is not the need for exact orthogonality. The original Muon already tolerates fairly inexact orthogonalization (e.g., mapping singular values only roughly into [1-ε,1+ε] with ε up to ~0.3). The real issue is that the input momentum matrix can be ill-conditioned with an unfavorable singular-value spectrum, slowing NS convergence. Muon2’s second-moment preconditioning empirically improves the spectrum/conditioning, which:
- speeds up NS convergence to a practically sufficient orthogonalization;
- improves directional alignment of the finite-iteration update with the “true” orthogonalized direction.
3) Metric shift: the paper argues that orthogonality error metrics (e.g., \|Q^TQ-I\|) alone do not capture what matters for optimization; directional alignment and finite-iteration utility are more relevant.
4) Muon2-F: a memory-efficient variant using a factorized second-moment preconditioner to avoid storing full second-moment tensors, retaining most of Muon2’s gains under large-scale memory constraints.

[skim: method overview]
Insert an Adam-like second-moment, per-parameter scaling right before Muon’s NS orthogonalization, making the matrix easier to orthogonalize so fewer NS steps are needed; provide a factorized-second-moment option to reduce memory.
summary_en.experiments: Across GPT-Small/Base/Large and LLaMA pre-training (≈60M–1B parameters), Muon2 and Muon2-F consistently outperform baselines while using ~40% fewer NS iterations per step, reducing compute/communication overhead. The paper also provides empirical evidence via spectral/conditioning and directional-alignment analyses supporting the chain: second-moment preconditioning → improved spectrum → faster NS convergence → better training outcomes.
summary_en.reading_guide:
[must_read: deep reading]
- Introduction: focus on the bottleneck framing (NS iterations) and the “good-enough orthogonalization” philosophy.
- The Muon2 Optimizer (Algorithm 1 + key equations, esp. the preconditioning equation and update scaling): understand precisely where second-moment scaling is inserted and how it changes the NS input.
- Analysis sections on conditioning/singular-value distributions and directional alignment (and why orthogonality error is insufficient): this is the core justification and conceptual novelty.
- Muon2-F: study how factorization is done, memory savings, and the performance trade-off.
- Experiments: prioritize (1) NS-iteration reduction and efficiency impact, (2) consistency across model scales, and (3) any plots/tables showing spectrum or alignment improvements.

[skim: quick reading]
Read Introduction + Algorithm/one key equation + main results tables + NS-iteration/efficiency comparisons; skim Muon2-F if you care about memory/engineering deployment.
summary_en.authors_note: The authors emphasize that optimization benefits come from improved update directions rather than strict orthogonality. Muon2 makes the NS orthogonalization easier by preconditioning the momentum with Adam-style second moments, enabling fewer NS iterations and better (or at least not worse) final performance; Muon2-F addresses memory overhead for large-scale training.

recommendation.zh: 这是少数直接打到预训练吞吐瓶颈的优化器改动；值得按他们的二阶矩自适应策略做端到端复现，验证能否在更少NS迭代下不掉loss曲线。
recommendation.en: One of the few optimizer tweaks that targets real pretrain throughput bottlenecks; worth an end-to-end repro to see if adaptive second-moment preconditioning preserves loss curves with fewer NS iterations.
